true_answer: 0.3. Sets 33 You might notice that the symbols for union and intersection slightly resemble the logic symbols for “or” and “and.” This is no accident. What does it mean for x to be an element of A ∪ B ? It means that x is an element of A or x is an element of B (or both). That is, x ∈ A ∪ B ⇔ x ∈ A ∨ x ∈ B . Similarly, x ∈ A ∩ B ⇔ x ∈ A ∧ x ∈ B . Also, x ∈ A ⇔ ¬( x ∈ A ) . which says x is an element of the complement of A if x is not an element of A . There is one more way to combine sets which will be useful for us: the Cartesian product , A × B .
